ai_summary: Great Britain is currently generating 14.2 GW of wind power, with estimated Scottish wind output contributing 3.6 GW, which accounts for 35.6% of installed Scottish wind capacity. This clean power has driven Scottish carbon intensity down to an impressive 0 gCO2/kWh, in stark contrast to the 52 gCO2/kWh recorded GB-wide. However, severe cross-border transmission constraints continue to prevent this zero-carbon energy from freely flowing south to major demand centers. As a direct result, 19.1 GWh of Scottish generation has been curtailed so far today through Balancing Mechanism bids, incurring a constraint cost of about £392,541. To replace this discarded renewable power, fossil-fuel plants elsewhere on the network were forced to burn an estimated 3,628,886 m3 of natural gas, releasing 6,685 tonnes of CO2 into the atmosphere. Annualised at current levels, the total yearly cost of Scottish curtailment is estimated at £143 million. Recovered through system balancing charges, this constraint burden adds an estimated £0.5/MWh to everybody's electricity invoice in the UK, underscoring the compounding economic and environmental price paid for delayed transmission upgrades.
